question: From a bus depot, buses leave every 8 minutes and travel along a straight road at a speed of 24 km/hr. A traveller moving towards the depot along the same road meets the buses at regular intervals of 6 minutes. Find the speed of the traveller.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance travelled by the bus in (8 − 6) = 2 minutes is exactly equal to the distance travelled by the traveller in 6 minutes.

So, Time taken by bus : Time taken by traveller = 2 : 6 = 1 : 3.

Since speed is inversely proportional to time, Speed of bus : Speed of traveller = 3 : 1.

Given speed of bus = 24 km/hr (which corresponds to 3 units).

Speed of traveller = 1 unit = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of bus (Sb) = 24 km/hr

Departure interval of buses = 8 minutes

Meeting interval = 6 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (opposite direction) = S₁ + S₂
